Subject: POC bootcamp and hands-on lab scheduling

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week — the execs liked what they saw and want to move into a hands-on POC bootcamp (we'll run a 1.5‑2 hour working session with our ML infra and product teams).

High level asks from our side:
- A session that covers prompt review, routing options, and a small load test (concurrency ~10, short bursts).
- A runbook / checklist for us to follow so the session is productive.
- We'll need to confirm the network/egress requirements with our security team.

Availability window: the week of May 10–14. We're Pacific time and prefer mornings. Any openings?

Jennifer

Hi Jennifer — thanks, glad the demo landed. Happy to run the bootcamp. Proposed approach and slots below.

Proposed session format (90–120 min):
- 15 min: intros & success criteria (we'll capture a mutual action list)
- 35–45 min: hands-on prompt & routing workshop (bring your sample prompts + use-cases)
- 20 min: controlled load test (we'll run short bursts to validate latency/cost)
- 10–20 min: next steps and rolloff (rollout plan, follow-ups)

Slot options (PT mornings):
- Tue May 11, 9:00–11:00am PT
- Wed May 12, 9:30–11:30am PT
- Thu May 13, 10:00–12:00pm PT

Prep I need from your side:
- One or two representative prompts/snippets (we'll sanity-check in advance)
- Approx expected concurrency for the load test and size of test dataset
- Any network constraints / egress policies we should know about

I'll attach a short runbook and a slide deck we typically use as pre-reads. Ben (SE) — can you prepare a lightweight load plan and a routing checklist we can share? Marissa — I'll loop you for meeting facilitation and success criteria capture.

If one of those slots works, I'll send a calendar invite and a prep pack (slides + runbook + checklist).

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jennifer Smith <jsmith@acmecorp.com>, ops@acmecorp.com
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC bootcamp and hands-on lab scheduling — technical checklist and load plan

Vivek / Marissa / Jennifer — quick technical checklist and asks from SE before the session. I'll attach a CSV load plan and a small routing map.

Key items for Acme infra: 
- Whitelist the Redwood public egress IP range we'll provide (or provide a NAT/IP allowlist entry).
- Ensure short-lived API key will be available for the load test (we'll use scoped key limited to token counts).
- Test dataset format: newline-delimited JSON, ~500 records, each record: {id, prompt}.
- Expected tokens per prompt: 60–150 tokens (we'll size batch windows accordingly).
- Concurrency target: 10 concurrent streams, 30s bursts, 3 repetitions with 60s gap for system cool-down.

What I'll share ahead: load-plan.csv (contains batch sizes, inter-burst timing), kv-routing-map.png (visual of fallback pathways), and a short checklist snippet that teams can gate on the day.

On the routing fallback question: we typically route by latency-first policy for bootcamp; if capacity is constrained we fall back to a compatible model variant (quantized / lower cost tier) in the same region. We'll demonstrate automatic fallback and how to pin model versions if you need strict determinism.

Attachments (stubs): load-plan.csv, kv-routing-map.png

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
